report.summary: EvolutionaryOrchestrator is real but incomplete. generate_candidates lacks timeout, evaluate_candidates uses binary pass/fail, select_best requires score>=100 (only perfect passes). Best-of-N baseline is misimplemented: it selects first among ties, not random. No mutation/selection loop exists. Highest-value next step: add per-candidate timeout to generate_candidates and implement a proper selection loop with configurable fitness threshold.
risks: generate_candidates has no timeout; a hanging agent blocks all candidates forever.
select_best requires score >= 100.0, so only perfect passes are considered; no partial credit.
Best-of-N baseline is not correctly implemented: ties are broken by sort stability (first in list), not random.
No mutation or iteration loop; this is a single-shot runner, not evolution.
evaluate_candidates uses binary pass/fail; intended replacement (evaluate_change) is not imported or used.
todos: Add per-candidate timeout in generate_candidates (asyncio.wait_for on manager.run_task).
Implement a proper selection loop: generate -> evaluate -> select -> mutate -> repeat.
Change select_best to handle ties randomly or by configurable strategy.
Add configuration for population size, mutation rate, and fitness threshold.

handoff.suggestion: The class is a scaffold. To make it real: (1) add timeout to generate_candidates, (2) implement a loop in a new method evolve() that calls generate, evaluate, select, and then mutates the best candidate (using a new mutate method on ShadowShellManager), (3) fix select_best to randomize ties, (4) replace binary pytest scoring with evaluate_change from daedalus.eval.correctness.
